name: Question 5
problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-4x(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(1) \\ y(1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] $$ Find the solution to the initial value problem above. *Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}].$*
$[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$ So, the matrix of the system is $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}].$

Given the system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as

$$
x(t)=Φ(t)\,c,
$$

where $Φ(t)$ is a fundamental matrix of the system, and $c$ is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as

$$
x(t)={Φ}_{0}(t)c={e}^{At}\,c,
$$

where ${Φ}_{0}(t)={e}^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting $t={t}_{0},$ we have

$$
x({t}_{0})={e}^{A{t}_{0}}\,c
$$

and since ${e}^{At}$ is invertible for all $t,$ we have

$$
c={e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}).
$$

Plugging the above back into our expression for $x(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,{e}^{-A{t}_{0}}\,x({t}_{0}) \\  & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}\,x({t}_{0}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{A(t-1)}\,x(1) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4(t-1)) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(4(t-1)) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(4(t-1)) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(4(t-1))\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(4(t-1))\, \\ \,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4(t-1))\,\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Writing our system in matrix form, we get x′(t)=[04−40]x(t), where x(t)=[x(t)y(t)]. So, the matrix of the system is A=[04−40].

Given the system x′(t)=Ax(t), where A is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as x(t)=Φ(t)c, where Φ(t) is a fundamental matrix of the system, and c is a constant vector.

So, we can write our general solution as x(t)=Φ0(t)c=eAtc, where Φ0(t)=eAt is the standard fundamental matrix of the system. Substituting t=t0, we have x(t0)=eAt0c and since eAt is invertible for all t, we have c=e−At0x(t0).

Plugging the above back into our expression for x(t), we get x(t)=eAte−At0x(t0)=eA(t−t0)x(t0).

Therefore, the solution is x(t)=eA(t−1)x(1)=[cos⁡(4(t−1))sin⁡(4(t−1))−sin⁡(4(t−1))cos⁡(4(t−1))][03]=[3sin⁡(4(t−1))3cos⁡(4(t−1))].
